subject: Re: Request to compress evaluation window and rephase close timeline
messages:

Cc: Acme Procurement <procure@acmepiping.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request to compress evaluation window and rephase close timeline

Logan —

Quick note from our side: procurement just surfaced an internal freeze that will block signatures for two weeks unless we can demonstrate a shortened evaluation window and a firm go/no-go cadence. We really like Redwood’s performance in the PoC so far, but the team needs a revised MAP that compresses the eval phase and gives procurement clearer gating checkpoints.

High level ask: can we compress the evaluation from 21 days to 10–12 days and align milestones so procurement can sign immediately after the acceptance gate? If that’s not possible, we need a formal escalation path we can present to our stakeholders.

I’ve copied our procurement inbox so they’re in the loop for timing.

Thanks,
Emily Larson
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Piping

Attachment: sample-runbook.pdf (stub)
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Emily Larson <emily.larson@acmepiping.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request to compress evaluation window and rephase close timeline

Emily —

Appreciate the heads up and the context. Short answer: yes, we can tighten the MAP but there are tradeoffs we should make explicit (reduced buffer for edge-case regressions, smaller parallel test coverage). Proposed next steps below — I can update the MAP and send a numbered action plan by EOD.

Proposed compressed timeline (10 business days):
- Day 0: MAP revision + kickoff call (we ship MAP_v3)
- Day 1–5: Focused perf + integration tests (we'll provide daily rollups)
- Day 6: Acceptance gate rehearsal with your SME
- Day 7–8: Final acceptance run and remediation window
- Day 9: Exec acceptance / sign-off window for procurement

Action items for us (Redwood):
- Update MAP with tighter milestones and a yes/no acceptance checklist (I’ll attach MAP_v3).
- Provide an executive-facing summary + one-slide decision memo for procurement.
- Stand up a 15-min daily sync during the compressed window.

Action items for Acme:
- Confirm the SME availability for Day 6 rehearsal.
- Share any procurement gating checklist items we must address ahead of acceptance.

I’m attaching a draft MAP (MAP_v3.xlsx) and a short procurement checklist template. If we get buy-in from procurement, we’ll also prepare a fallback: a documented escalation route that triggers an SLA exception and exec review if any acceptance criteria miss their window.

Would you like us to schedule the kickoff for Monday at 9am PT?

—Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_v3.xlsx (stub); procurement_checklist.pdf (stub)

Logan / Emily —

Procurement can accept an accelerated window provided we receive: (1) a clear acceptance checklist in advance, (2) a DocuSign-ready agreement with payment terms defined, and (3) a named exec escalation contact from Redwood should any acceptance criteria fail.

We can make signature priority if the acceptance gate is strictly documented and our legal team gets the contract draft by Day 7 of the compressed plan. Please include estimated risk and mitigation notes in the contract annex.

Regards,
Acme Procurement Team

Cc: Emily Larson <emily.larson@acmepiping.com>, Acme Procurement <procure@acmepiping.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 12:34:00 -0700
Subject: Escalation prep — compressed window risk assessment

Team —

I ran a quick risk assessment for the compressed 10-day eval window. Summary: doable, but categorized as HIGH risk relative to our standard 21-day MAP. Key concerns: limited remediation time for model edge cases, integration testing may surface infra flakiness, and we have a smaller window to validate quantized model artifacts.

Recommended mitigations (short):
- Put a hard stop on non-blocking feature tests until after acceptance.
- Reserve a 48-hour emergency remediation buffer (we call this the "mini-sprint") that can be converted to an SLA exception if needed.
- Assign an on-call Redwood engineer for Days 4–9 for immediate triage.

I recommend we escalate to Sales Leadership for pre-approval of a one-week discretionary remediation credit and to name the exec contact for Acme procurement. If leadership approves, we can present a single-slide "escalation play" that reads cleanly to Acme execs.

Priya
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: Exec ask: approval for one-week remediation credit & named escalation for ACME-4521

Marissa —

Acme (ACME-4521) is asking us to compress their evaluation timeline to ~10 business days to unlock signage during a procurement freeze window. Priya's assessment flags this as HIGH risk; the recommended mitigations require an on-call engineer and a one-week discretionary remediation credit (to be used only if acceptance fails and remediation is required). Procurement also wants a named exec contact for escalation.

Why this matters: if we push back, Acme will likely move to another vendor for the quarter. If we approve, we can capture the deal this quarter but accept measurable risk on our delivery margin.

Ask: approve (A) a one-week remediation credit, (B) naming Marissa Cole as the exec escalation contact, and (C) greenlight for legal to prioritize a DocuSign-ready draft to match the compressed MAP.

If approved I will send Acme a one-slide escalation play and updated MAP_v3 with the acceptance checklist.

Thanks,
Logan
